kill_condition.text: If R1 or R2 fails, the surviving compute saving does not scale into the regime where it would matter, and the adaptive-compute programme is finished with no result worth an architecture.
reasoning: R1 failed, so the kill condition fires and QNEURO3-PARETO-P1 is dead. It is NOT re-issued and
its numbers may not be cited as a confirmed prediction.
It would be easy to argue the kill should be waived because R1 failed only in the direction of
arrival being better. That argument is declined. A kill condition that is waived when the
outcome is flattering is not a kill condition, and this programme has already paid for that
The follow-up matched-accuracy measurement is recorded separately under QNEURO3-NICHE-001 as a

what_R3_uncovered: Diagnosing R3 produced the most useful finding of the branch. The batched forward pass runs
every step and then selects, so the saving was nominal. Implementing genuine early exit and
benchmarking a TRAINED model gives 4.89x at batch 1 and 0.96-0.99x at batch 64-256.
The mechanism is analytic: a batch cannot exit until its slowest member does, so batched cost
scales with E[max halt over the batch], not E[halt]. See QNEURO3-NICHE-001.
